title: Auto Loans: The Autopay Discount in an Enrolled Rate
content:
Whether the autopay discount is part of the rate written when an Auto Loans account is enrolled in autopay depends on one fact about the loan: how many days past due it shows at that moment.

## Rule

The enrolled rate includes the autopay discount only when the loan record shows zero days past due, meaning that no installment is past due, at the time the enrollment is recorded. A rate written with an enrollment made while an installment is past due leaves the autopay discount out. A loan that is enrolled again after its autopay was cancelled gets the discount back on the same single condition as an original enrollment: zero days past due.

The paying account has no say in this. Every enrollment has to draw on an active checking account in the borrower's own name, so the account the borrower names settles where installments will be taken from and nothing else; it never decides whether the discount is in the rate.

The count of days past due is taken from the loan record as it reads when the enrollment is recorded.

## Truth table

| Days past due on the loan record when the enrollment is recorded | Autopay discount in the enrolled rate |
|---|---|
| zero | included |
| one or more | not included |

## Basis Q&A

**Does it matter which of the borrower's checking accounts is named to pay?** Not for the discount. It matters only for where the installments are drawn.

**Is the test the loan's delinquent status or its past-due installments?** The test is the day count on the loan record: the discount needs zero days past due.
